title: Fiber Paths and Physical-Layer Reliability
summary: Analyze labeled synthetic fiber paths, degradation indicators, and qualified-handling boundaries.
objectives: Trace a documented fiber path and interpret synthetic loss or error indicators.
Recognize when physical handling requires qualified supervision and escalation.

vocab.def: The documented route used to carry signals through fiber components.
A decline in signal or service quality shown by evidence.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: Never look into active fiber, disconnect live optical systems, splice fiber, or perform facility cabling work. Use records and synthetic indicators only.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Accessible path description: Rack A port 12 connects through Patch Panel P1 to Fiber Route F-02, then to Rack B port 7. A parallel route F-03 uses a separate documented path. Compare labels, endpoint records, error counts, and path notes before proposing escalation.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Document source, destination, labels, observed indicators, uncertainty, and the qualified role that should handle physical inspection.

practice.prompt: What is the safe response to a possible live-fiber issue?
practice.answer: Do not inspect or handle it; preserve the record and escalate to a qualified authorized role.

quiz.question: What should a learner do with a possible active-fiber degradation?
options: Document synthetic or provided evidence and escalate
Look into the fiber to inspect it
quiz.answer: Document synthetic or provided evidence and escalate

lab.objective: Document a synthetic fiber path and safe escalation.

reflectionPrompt: Which path facts were documented, and which physical checks were outside scope?

careerConnection.text: This is supervised educational infrastructure practice, not professional qualification.
